newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - August 6.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - August 6.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

DALLAS - Compaq Computer Corp plans an estimated $20 million plus fall advertising campaign to target consumers who have yet to buy PCs. Three 30-second commercials have been created by agency Ammirati Puris Lintas, New York, which won Compaq's $200 million worldwide account in May.

PARIS - French state airline Air France says it has awarded its world advertising business to Ammirati Puris Lintas following a public tender launched in February. The purchasing of advertising space has been awarded to Mediapolis, a subsidiary of Havas Advertising, it says.

LONDON - WPP Plc, the world's largest advertising and marketing services group, says it has bought 69.73 percent of French direct marketing agency BFA for 26.82 million French francs ($4.2 million) in cash.
OAK BROOK, Illinois - McDonald's Corp is pairing with Kellogg Co in a cross-promotion that features coupons for McDonald's food items on 14 varieties of Kellogg's cereal, the companies announce.

LONDON - Britain's top advertising trade organisation says the country's Labour government is proving sympathetic to the industry, although there are concerns about a proposal to create a food standards agency.
MUNICH - The future of television advertising lies in a mixture of new technology and traditional TV commercials, says German television group ProSieben Media AG.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:
PARIS - French pay-television group Canal Plus is in talks with newspaper publishers Groupe Amaury to set up a television news channel to rival LCI of TF1, says the La Tribune newspaper.
NEW DELHI - India says a bill seeking to allow private broadcasters to beam radio and television programmes from the country is likely to be approved by parliament late this year.

LONDON - Channel 5, Britain's newest terrestrial television channel, says it struck a three-year deal with the British Fashion Council for exclusive rights to broadcast the Lloyds Bank British Fashion Awards. The station has also acquired the rights to London soccer team Arsenal's home matches in Europe's UEFA Cup in the coming season, it says.
WASHINGTON - MCI Communications Corp and privately held Progressive Networks Inc say they will offer a service to deliver audio and video to broadcast-size audiences over the Internet.
LONDON - British media company Chrysalis Group Plc says it is buying Faze FM Radio Ltd, the owner of Kiss 102 and Kiss 105 radio stations, for 17.5 million pounds ($28.4 million) in cash.

MAINZ - Germany avoids becoming the first advanced country to tax people who have PCs connected to the Internet. After threatening to hit Internet PCs with the same fee now charged for owning a television, representatives of German state governments bow to pressure from politicians in Bonn and say they will not impose the tax.

LONDON - Cyber shopping, in which music, holidays and groceries can be bought over the Internet, may gain wider acceptance following news that a secure system of payment is now available, says a report.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

LONDON - Anglo-Dutch consumer group Unilever Plc NV is set on expansion in the developing and emerging markets of the Far East and Latin America, says chairman Niall Fitzgerald. Current policy is to look for areas where the company could find "incremental growth," he says.

MUNICH - Adidas AG says second quarter net income rose 20 percent to 69 million marks ($36.7 million) behind a 37 percent rise in net sales to 1.427 billion marks, particularly in North America where it has begun reaping the benefits of an aggressive advertising campaign. Apparel remained the major growth driver for the brand in the first six months of 1997. Footwear, helped the most by running shoes, rose 29 percent and outperformed the market.

LONDON - British soft drinks to chocolate group Cadbury-Schweppes says its core 7-Up brand has grown in the six months to June 14 while sales of Dr Pepper rose 4.3 percent. The group plans to spend more than 350 million pounds on marketing in the second half of 1997, with the launch of a national television campaign in Britain for a new biscuit snack called Astros, says chief executive John Sunderland.

HONG KONG - Dickson Concepts, the luxury goods retailer, says it intends to open about 100 new shops internationally during the current financial year. Chairman Dickson Poon says the company has also signed a franchise agreement with Brooks Brothers, a wholly owned unit of Marks and Spencer Plc, to exclusively operate Brooks Brothers stores in South East Asia.

PARIS - California-based computer technology company Bay Networks Inc., the third-largest maker of computer networking gear, is expecting further rapid sales growth in Europe, says Alain Sanchez, marketing director France.

BOLOGNA - Conserve Italia says it is to acquire France's Verjame SA, the country's leading fruit conserver. Conserve Italia, which owns the brands Valfrutta, Yoga, Derby, Jolly Colombani and Mon Jardin, says the purchase would create Europe's leading group in the sector.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

LONDON - British men are spending more money than ever before on toiletries, fuelled by changing attitudes to image and crafty marketing by manufacturers, according to new report. The British market for men's toiletries this year is expected to reach about 753 million pounds, market research group Euromonitor says.

DUESSELDORF - German teenagers have become media and advertising experts, using or ignoring offers at will, says a study by the German unit of advertising group Grey. In contrast to Generation X, those in their late 20s who rejected advertising and mass consumption, teenagers today have learned to weed through the growing quantity because they have grown up a plethora of television channels and Internet, says the report.

TOKYO - American mega-mall developers, lured by visions of well-heeled Japanese consumers with a yen for one-stop shopping, see potential profits in a market once dominated by tiny family-run stores. Experts say Japan is in the throes of a retail revolution which promises more and bigger shopping centres likely to lure growing numbers of foreign retailers.
